subject: Orion Retail — POC capacity & success criteria
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Orion Retail — POC capacity & success criteria

Thanks again for the call this morning — good discussion and lots of alignment. Quick written recap and proposed plan so we can lock dates. Attaching a capacity estimate and our POC playbook for reference.

Summary / goals
- Primary objective: validate inference economics and latency for Orion's checkout recommendation flow (average prompt ~320 tokens, heavy burst windows during promotions).
- Success criteria (proposed):
  - p95 latency <= 200ms for 512-token generation under 95th percentile traffic patterns
  - Sustained throughput: 10 requests/sec with 100ms inter-request jitter for 30-minute windows
  - Model quality: top-3 recommendation match rate within 5% of current prod baseline on provided evaluation set
  - Cost target: unit cost per 1k generated tokens below $0.60 (post-quantization/config)

POC scope and capacity proposal
- Duration: 3 weeks of active evaluation + 1 week ramp/down (total 4 weeks). Target start: 2026-09-01 (flexible).
- Baseline reserved capacity: 2 x A100-equivalent GPUs dedicated to your POC (keeps KV cache warm for low-latency tail).
- Autoscaling policy: up to 6 GPUs for sustained load spikes; burst to 8 GPUs for short promotional events (max burst 10 minutes) — policy uses queue-depth + token-rate triggers.
- Expected warm-up behavior: cold-start for new sessions ~300-400ms on first token; with reserved GPUs and prefix caching we expect warm sessions to hit p95 target.

Evaluation plan / ownership
- Orion provides: evaluation prompts (sample set), 2 representative production traces (anonymized), and a demo account/endpoint to run inference harness.
- Redwood provides: ingress test harness (load generator), prebuilt evaluation scripts, and dashboard with token-level cost and latency metrics.
- Owners: Dev Patel (SE) — infra/config & kickoff; Hannah Schmitt (AE) — commercial/contract coordination; Marcus Lin (SA) — runtime tuning and config.

Next steps proposed
1) Confirm POC start date (target 2026-09-01).
2) Orion to send evaluation dataset + anonymized trace by 2026-08-24.
3) We will provision reserved GPUs and share the runtime config (poc-runtime-config.yaml) before kickoff.
4) Sign minimal SOW (DocuSign link below) to enable reserved capacity provisioning.

Attachments: Orion_POC_capacity_estimate.xlsx, redwood_poc_playbook.pdf
DocuSign SOW: https://www.docusign.net/Signing/?s=ABCDEF123456
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/company/Orion-Retail-OR-456

Thanks — happy to adjust success criteria if the team prefers different thresholds.

—

Hi Lauren — quick technical answers and config notes.

Autoscaling & billing
- Reserved 2 GPUs: billed as the monthly commitment for the POC (we'll invoice pro rata for the POC window once SOW is signed).
- Autoscale increments (3-6 GPUs): billed as short-term metered capacity on top of reserved. Burst (7-8 GPUs) is also metered; we can apply a short-term burst credit if you prefer (requires sales approval).

Placement & latency
- We recommend colocating reserved GPUs in a single AZ to minimize intra-cluster network hops and KV cache variance. Autoscaling nodes may come from the same AZ where capacity is available; we will bias scheduling to keep nodes local when possible.

Security / data handling
- Evaluation traces are loaded into a dedicated ephemeral namespace for the POC. No traces are written to shared long-term storage by default. Any logs that leave the runtime are scrubbed/anonymized; we can provide an export of the scrubber rules. If you require VPC-private deployment for the POC, Redwood Private can be stood up (longer lead time).

Dataset format checklist
- Preferred: JSON Lines, one record per inference call, fields: input_text, context_metadata (optional), expected_output (if available).
- Alternative: CSV with quoted fields — ensure newlines in payloads are escaped.
- Please anonymize user IDs and any PII; hashed IDs are OK.

Attached: poc-runtime-config.yaml (sample runtime config we'll apply at kickoff). Highlights: KV cache TTL, batch-size target, autoscale thresholds, burst duration cap. Small notes inline in the file.

Happy to do a short technical sync (30m) with your SREs pre-kickoff to walk through the config.

—Marcus

- Metered autoscale / burst: metered at per-GPU-hour on top of reservation.
- If procurement needs a cap, we can set a hard spend cap on the account and alert if forecasted usage hits 70%.

Procurement items we need to proceed
1) Signed SOW (link: https://www.docusign.net/Signing/?s=ABCDEF123456) — this unlocks reserved capacity provisioning.
2) PO number (if required) or internal approval note — Hannah will coordinate commercial terms.
3) Dataset + traces by 2026-08-24 to meet a 2026-09-01 kickoff.

Kickoff agenda (30–60m) proposed

- POC success criteria & acceptance tests (10m)
- Runtime config review & autoscale triggers (15m)
- Data handoff and evaluation runbook (10m)

Thanks — looping Hannah for SOW/PO coordination.
